title: NGAP: support non standard implementation of NRPPa encapsulation
description:
The standard is quite clear that NRPPa PDU must be encoded inside
ngap.NRPPa-PDU ASN1 type.

However a well known vendor bypass this and encode the data directly as
nrppa.NRPPA-PDU ASN1 type.

Add an option to support this non standard implementation.

notes.body: Not sure why the pipeline failes. Maybe something with your git account.

The parameter description is very unclear. It might be better to explicitly indicate the vendor using this buggy implementation so that people have a chance to know when to toggle it exactly.
Given that NRPPa is between the gNB and core network, I really wonder how they expect to have a proper interworking anyway as a valid gNB will fail to decode the message. Is this really deployed in the field?

Hello,

The problem happens with Huawei AMF on the NL1 interface (NRPPa over HTTP2).

The NG-C link is fine and aligned with Wireshark.

To be honest, there is a contradiction in the standard between 3GPP 38.305 and 3GPP TS 29.518.

In 3GPP 38.305 v17 - section 6.5.1 (Stage 2), which is high level, we only see NRPPa layer without NGAP.

![2025-01-28T11_53_54+01_00_capture](/uploads/61f94761ffcb6b245950fc0ad91d4489/2025-01-28T11_53_54+01_00_capture.png)

But we believe that 3GPP TS 29.518 is clear about the usage of NGAP IE, we checked from the first version to the last version of the standard.
![2025-01-28T12_24_53+01_00_capture](/uploads/c3f0ae5b3885947ab76f22929f2245d4/2025-01-28T12_24_53+01_00_capture.png)

As you said 38.305 is a high level drawing while 29.518 gives the technical details for implementation so there is no doubt on what to do.
The MR should be updated so as to have a more meaningful parameter and likely an expert info indicating that this is a invalid PDU while still attempting the decoding.
This also means that Huawei LMF can only work with Huawei AMF, otherwise you have an interoperability issue.I guess you are using both components from Huawei?

I found out that Huawei submitted a change request to 3GPP in April 2024 but it was postponed because Nokia said it would cause interoperability problems.

So now it looks clear to me that the two incompatible behaviors are live, but not in the same MNO.
If each MNO has only one AMF vendor, and if they choose a matching or configurable LMF, it can work...

I'm not very keen on this change. Huawei should fix their code to comply with the standard. Wireshark should veryfy the corectness of protocol as it is a protocol analyser. At the very least it should higlight that this is a protocol error.
Here is another variant of the patch that automatically detects the problem and highlight that this is a protocol error.
The heuristic does not seem strong enough to me so having people explicitly activating it with a preference + an expert info when it is on would seem better to me. @AndersBroman what do you think?

Maybe some explanation about the heuristic.
When NRPPA-PDU is not encapsulated, it starts with 0 (initiatingMessage) or 1 or 2.
When it is encapsulated, it starts with the pdu length, not counting the byte length.
And successfulOutcome or unsuccessfulOutcome require more than 1 or 2 bytes.

```
NRPPA-PDU ::= CHOICE {
        initiatingMessage               InitiatingMessage,
        successfulOutcome               SuccessfulOutcome,
        unsuccessfulOutcome     UnsuccessfulOutcome,
        ...
}
```
We should not have a heuristic to ensure that an invalid payload is detected as such by default.

What about a try catch block, which mentions the preference in the fault
case.  If the preference is enabled add a waring about faulty
implementation?

skrev:
What about yesterday version then ?
Version 2 sounds good to me. @AndersBroman is it ok for you?
Yes
Do I have to do something ? Repush version 2 ?
Yes that's correct.
Done
